name: Mecca Normal
label: K
lede: [[Jean Smith]] sings, [[David Lester]] plays guitar, and nobody else is invited; [[Kathleen Hanna]] says she wouldn't be in a band if she hadn't heard of Smith.

eras.title: A newspaper office, a borrowed practice room
eras.text: A graphic designer and a poet meet at a Vancouver left-wing paper, start a band with one guitar and one voice, press their own LP and drive it south. Nobody's permission is asked at any point.

q: The main thing is, you didn't ask for permission. You didn't play the capitalist game.
years.src: Throwaway Style: The Early Years of Mecca Normal · Mecca Normal - Wikipedia · David Lester (musician) - Wikipedia · Jean Smith (singer) - Wikipedia
years.h: Smith and Lester meet at a Vancouver paper and start a duo
years.p: [[Jean Smith|56b2d08f-076e-4c81-bb6e-9d7cdab65bb1]] and [[David Lester|b6f927cf-2825-4bdb-b4cf-ece5a8da88f0]] form Mecca Normal with one guitar and one voice. It stays a duo, with no drums on record until well into the 1990s.
years.xp:
Lester was working as a graphic designer for the leftist paper Open Road when he met Smith at another local newspaper office. They bonded over local shows before they bonded over a band.

"The main thing is, you didn't ask for permission. You didn't play the capitalist game," Lester told KEXP. Sources disagree on the start date: K Records and Wikipedia's band page say 1984, while the Smith and Lester biographies on Wikipedia say 1981.

years.src: Throwaway Style: The Early Years of Mecca Normal
years.h: A duo with no drummer opens for D.O.A.
years.p: Lester's brother Ken managed the Vancouver hardcore band [[D.O.A.|0f0b2f97-a073-4a92-ab99-ff7980ad7fca]] from 1979, which is how a guitar and a voice landed a first gig on a punk bill.
years.xp: D.O.A. and the Subhumans were the city's politically engaged punk bands, and Mecca Normal came out of the same scene with far less volume. The show is undated in the sources we found.

years.src: Artistic Independence and Social Media: Interview with DIY Multimedia Icon Jean Smith · Throwaway Style: The Early Years of Mecca Normal · Mecca Normal | Trouser Press
years.h: The first LP is cut in a borrowed practice room
years.p: Mecca Normal comes out on Smarten Up!, the imprint that grew out of Smith's zine. Trouser Press notes it was made on a cassette 4-track.
years.xp: Smith's zine Smarten Up! became the label for their first record after very few local shows. Trouser Press singles out two songs that became live staples, "Are You Hungry Joe?" and "I Walk Alone." K reissued the album in 1995.

years.src: Normal History Vol. 898: The Art Of David Lester
years.h: Expo 86 evicts Vancouver's poorest postal code, and D.O.A. answers with a seven-inch
years.p: Mecca Normal contributes a song to the D.O.A. protest record about evictions ahead of the fair.
years.xp: According to Magnet's history column, a benefit concert in Stanley Park with D.O.A., Pete Seeger and Arlo Guthrie raised $10,000 for people who lost their housing.

years.src: Throwaway Style: The Early Years of Mecca Normal · Mecca Normal - K Records · Artistic Independence and Social Media: Interview with DIY Multimedia Icon Jean Smith
years.h: Calvin Johnson trades a Beat Happening LP for the Mecca Normal debut
years.p: At GESSCO in Olympia, on the Black Wedge tour, [[Calvin Johnson|cac7a688-14a8-46c3-8fc8-11cca866677c]] swaps [[Beat Happening|449e44cb-bcae-4c48-a1af-5d8df0f81456]]'s self-titled record for Mecca Normal's.
years.xp:
Smith and Lester co-founded Black Wedge in 1986, a touring bundle of anti-authoritarian poets and minimalist musicians, and borrowed D.O.A.'s bus to cover the west coast and the American heartland.

Smith was wary of the yellow Beat Happening album, which shows a cat riding a rocket, and it warped on the bus. Johnson still invited the band to contribute "Smile Baby" to K's cassette compilation Let's Sea, and that is how the K relationship starts.

eras.title: K Records takes them in
eras.text: Two records for K Records, the second cut in Olympia, and a week in 1991 when a whole generation of girl bands turns out to have been listening.

years.src: Mecca Normal | Trouser Press · Throwaway Style: The Early Years of Mecca Normal · Mecca Normal - K Records
years.h: Calico Kills the Cat, first record for K (KLP004)
years.p: A studio that suits Smith's low register better than the debut's cassette 4-track.
years.xp: Trouser Press hears "the seeds of Mecca Normal's future" in it. K reissued it in November 2024.

years.src: Mecca Normal | Trouser Press · Mecca Normal, "Water Cuts My Hands"! · Water Cuts My Hands [KLP008], by Mecca Normal
years.h: Johnson and Maley record Water Cuts My Hands in Olympia
years.p: Johnson and engineer Patrick Maley work the board, and K and Matador release it together.
years.xp: K calls it the band's third album. Smith described the title song as an encounter with a street person that leaves a woman wondering why her empathy doesn't override his misogyny. The Village Voice wrote in 1990: "I don't know of any other rock 'n' roll so closely attuned to the realities of women's rage."

years.big: "It makes me wanna cry, I am glad they exist."
q: I wouldn't be in a band if I hadn't heard of Jean.
years.src: Mecca Normal, "Water Cuts My Hands"! · Artistic Independence and Social Media: Interview with DIY Multimedia Icon Jean Smith · Throwaway Style: The Early Years of Mecca Normal
years.h: Hanna hears them and wants to cry
years.p: [[Kathleen Hanna|4638653b-a279-42d6-bd8c-b2bcb9a19f77]] of [[Bikini Kill|1397d045-1603-41fc-80b9-712c18360145]] on Mecca Normal in 1991, as K Records' write-up has it.
years.xp: In a later interview Hanna is quoted saying she wouldn't be in a band if she hadn't heard of Smith. Smith has said Hanna and Tobi Vail have mentioned Mecca Normal as significant, and that between songs she encouraged women to start bands.

years.src: International Pop Underground Convention - Wikipedia · Artistic Independence and Social Media: Interview with DIY Multimedia Icon Jean Smith
years.h: Smith plays opening night at the Olympia convention
years.p: The International Pop Underground Convention starts with a showcase for female punk and queercore acts, and [[Jean Smith|56b2d08f-076e-4c81-bb6e-9d7cdab65bb1]] is on it.
years.xp:
The festival ran August 20-25, 1991, centered on the Capitol Theater, with about fifty bands including [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]], Bikini Kill and Melvins. Passes were $35 for five days, according to organizer Candice Pedersen.

The opening night was called Love Rock Revolution Girl Style Now, and it became a reference point for riot grrrl.

eras.title: Matador signs them, and a drummer sits in
eras.text: K puts out three more records and a singles compilation, Smith publishes her first novel, and a move to Matador brings a third musician for the first time.

years.src: Mecca Normal | Trouser Press · Mecca Normal - K Records
years.h: Dovetail gives Lester's guitar a melodic side
years.p: Johnson and Maley produce again in Olympia, and the record is K's KLP014.
years.xp: Trouser Press credits Smith with "increasing control as a vocalist" on the record.

years.src: Mecca Normal | Trouser Press · Mecca Normal - K Records
yt: Full set at Jabberjaw, Los Angeles, Feb 12, 1994
years.p: K's KLP018 compilation, which Trouser Press calls the record that best captures the band's pull between anger and beauty.
years.xp: Flood Plain (KLP022) arrived the same year, a studio album on which Trouser Press finds the duo "in closer synch than ever." The video is a 48-minute set at Jabberjaw in Los Angeles in February 1994.

years.h: Smith publishes a novel, I Can Hear Me Fine
years.p: Independent presses issue her first book in 1993; The Ghost of Understanding follows in 1998.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the second novel incorporates lyrics from several Mecca Normal albums. Smith received Canada Council for the Arts awards in 2000 and 2007.

years.src: Sitting on Snaps - Wikipedia · Mecca Normal | Trouser Press
yt: This is Different, live in San Francisco
years.h: Matador's first Mecca Normal record divides the critics
years.p: [[Peter Jefferies|20a3f1b5-2c27-491d-a5a6-3f61ae253edd]] of New Zealand plays piano on "Cyclone" and "Vacant Night Sky" on Sitting on Snaps, and Johnson produces some tracks.
years.xp:
Rolling Stone called it "free punk," the Los Angeles Times put Smith's voice in "a space between Grace Slick, Patti Smith and a dental drill," Option called it "highly unlistenable," and Robert Christgau gave it a dud.

The same year Smith formed 2 Foot Flame with Jefferies and Michael Morley of the Dead C, also on Matador.

years.src: Mecca Normal | Trouser Press · Mecca Normal - Wikipedia
years.h: Jefferies drums on seven songs of The Eagle and the Poodle
years.p: Seven of the thirteen tracks have a drummer, the closest Mecca Normal comes to a trio.
years.xp: Trouser Press finds it "surprising how little" the third member changes the band's sound. Who Shot Elvis? followed on Matador in 1997.

eras.title: A lecture tour with amplifiers
eras.text: Through the 2000s the band plays clubs, classrooms and bookstores, signs to Kill Rock Stars, and turns the show into a talk.

years.src: Artistic Independence and Social Media: Interview with DIY Multimedia Icon Jean Smith · Mecca Normal - Wikipedia
years.h: Classrooms, galleries and bookstores join the club circuit
years.p: Mecca Normal builds "How Art & Music Can Change the World," a lecture-performance for rooms that aren't clubs.
years.xp: The 2009 twenty-fifth anniversary tour split its dates between conventional venues and educational spaces, according to Smith's interview with Tamra Lucid. The Family Swan came out on Kill Rock Stars in 2002 and Janis Zeppelin on Smarten Up! in 2003.

years.cap: Jean Smith and David Lester at The Green House, Arcata, California
years.src: Mecca Normal - Wikipedia · David Lester (musician) - Wikipedia · Artistic Independence and Social Media: Interview with DIY Multimedia Icon Jean Smith
years.h: After online dating, an album: The Observer
years.p: Smith's experiences on dating websites inspire the Kill Rock Stars record.
years.xp:
The Globe and Mail named Lester among ten famous Canadians you've never heard of in 2007.

The 2009 twenty-fifth anniversary tour split its dates between conventional venues and educational spaces, according to Smith's interview with Tamra Lucid.

eras.title: Still going, and drawing
eras.text: A new record, a painting series sold one portrait at a time, and a reissue that finally puts the K catalogue online.

years.cap: Mecca Normal live at the Media Club, Vancouver
years.h: Empathy for the Evil arrives on M'lady's Records
years.p: The 2014 album follows a run of live dates, still with one guitar and one voice.

years.src: Water Cuts My Hands [KLP008], by Mecca Normal · Mecca Normal, "Water Cuts My Hands"! · Throwaway Style: The Early Years of Mecca Normal · Jean Smith (singer) - Wikipedia · David Lester (musician) - Wikipedia
years.h: K puts Water Cuts My Hands online for the first time
years.p: The album goes digital on June 13, 2025, ahead of a vinyl and digital reissue, with a video that features Smith's painting.
years.xp: Smith has been selling 11x14 inch acrylic portraits through Facebook for $100 each since 2016, aiming to fund a free artist residency. Lester illustrated the 2019 graphic novel 1919: A Graphic History of the Winnipeg General Strike.
